Either one being off disables auto-flush.\npub fn enabled(config: &Config, no_auto_flush_flag: bool) -> bool {\n    config.sync.auto_flush && !no_auto_flush_flag\n}\n\n/// Outcome of an auto-flush attempt, ready to bridge into the warning channel.\n///\n/// Only [`FlushOutcome::Failed`] surfaces a warning — a disabled or successful\n/// flush is silent (`warning()` returns `None`).\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum FlushOutcome {\n    /// Auto-flush was disabled (config off or `--no-auto-flush`); only `Failed` yields `Some`.\n    pub fn warning(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        match self {\n            FlushOutcome::Failed(msg) => Some(msg.as_str()),\n            FlushOutcome::Disabled | FlushOutcome::Flushed(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of beads flushed, or `0` when disabled/failed.\n    pub fn flushed_count(&self) -> usize {\n        match self {\n            FlushOutcome::Flushed(n) => *n,\n            FlushOutcome::Disabled | FlushOutcome::Failed(_) => 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the flush was attempted and failed.\n    pub fn is_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, FlushOutcome::Failed(_))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Perform the dirty-only flush of `workspace_dir`'s beads to JSONL.\n///\n/// Thin wrapper over [`crate::sync::flush_dirty`]; }\n}\n\n/// Convenience wrapper that resolves enablement from `config` + the CLI flag\n/// via [`enabled`] before delegating to [`after_mutation`].\npub fn after_mutation_with_config(\n cmd_init(beads_dir: &PathBuf, prefix: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(beads_dir)?;\n\n    let config_path = beads_dir.join(\"config.yaml\");\n    if !config_path.exists() {\n \"issues.jsonl\"}\"#;\n        std::fs::write(&metadata_path, metadata)?;\n    }\n\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(\"beads.db\");\n    let _storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n\n    let println!(\"Initialized bead-forge workspace in {:?}\", beads_dir);\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Best-effort SQLite→JSONL flush after a SUCCESSFUL single-issue mutation.\n///\n/// This is the shared wiring for Phase 7.1 child 2/5 (bf-3iosi): every\n/// single-issue mutation handler calls this once its storage write has\n/// committed. It honors the effective auto-flush switch\n/// (`config.sync.auto_flush && !--no-auto-flush`) via child 1's\n/// [`crate::autoflush::after_mutation_with_config`].\n///\n/// A flush failure NEVER fails the mutation — the write already succeeded and\n/// the flush layer retains the `dirty_issues` marks so the next flush (or\n/// `bf sync --flush-only`) recovers. On failure we emit a stderr warning and\n/// return the warning text so a `--json` caller can also fold it into its\n/// output envelope via [`crate::format::with_warning`]. Returns `None` when\n/// auto-flush is disabled or the flush succeeded.\nfn autoflush_after_mutation(\n    beads_dir: &Path,\n    config: &Config,\n    no_auto_flush: bool,\n) -> Option<String> {\n    let outcome = crate::autoflush::after_mutation_with_config(beads_dir, config, no_auto_flush);\n    surface_flush_outcome(&outcome)\n}\n\n/// Like [`autoflush_after_mutation`] but for a hard delete: prunes the deleted\n/// beads' now-stale lines from JSONL via [`crate::autoflush::after_delete`]\n/// (the FK cascade drops their `dirty_issues` rows, so an ordinary dirty flush\n/// could never remove them). Best-effort — a flush failure never fails the\n/// delete; it degrades to a stderr warning and the returned text.\nfn autoflush_after_delete(\n    beads_dir: &Path,\n    config: &Config,\n crate::autoflush::after_delete(beads_dir, enabled, removed_ids);\n    surface_flush_outcome(&outcome)\n}\n\n/// Bridge a [`crate::autoflush::FlushOutcome`] into the user-facing warning\n/// channel: &crate::autoflush::FlushOutcome) -> Option<String> {\n    match outcome.warning() {\n        Some(w) => {\n            crate::format::warn_stderr(w);\n            Some(w.to_string())\n        }\n        None => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn cmd_create(\n    beads_dir: &PathBuf,\n    title: String,\n    type_: String,\n    priority: i32,\n    description: Option<String>,\n    assignee: Option<String>,\n    labels: Vec<String>,\n    json: bool,\n    no_auto_flush: bool,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let config = load_config(beads_dir)?;\n    let metadata = load_metadata(beads_dir)?;\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n    let storage = Storage::open_with_config(&db_path, &config)?;\n\n    let count = storage.count_issues()?;\n    let prefix = get_default_prefix(&config);\n\n    let mut issue = Issue::new(String::new(), title, \".\".to_string());\n    issue.issue_type = IssueType::from_str(type_.as_str()).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?;\n    issue.priority = Priority(priority);\n    issue.description = description;\n    // Normalize empty/whitespace-only to None so `bf create --assignee ''`\n    // creates a bead with no assignee instead of a literal empty string.\n    issue.assignee = normalize_assignee(assignee.as_deref());\n    issue.labels = labels;\n\n    // Short IDs are sized for ~1% collision probability by design\n    // (id::optimal_hash_length), so a colliding INSERT is an expected\n    // event: re-roll the ID instead of failing the create.\n    let mut id = String::new();\n    let mut created = false;\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for _ in 0..5 {\n        id = crate::id::generate_id(prefix, count);\n        issue.id = id.clone();\n        match storage.create_issue(&issue) {\n            Ok(()) => {\n                created = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            Err(e)\n                if e.to_string()\n                    .contains(\"UNIQUE constraint failed: issues.id\") =>\n            {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    if !created {\n        return Err(last_err.unwrap_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"ID collision retries exhausted\")));\n    }\n\n    // Incremental flush of the just-created bead (best effort; never fatal).\n    let warning = autoflush_after_mutation(beads_dir, &config, no_auto_flush);\n\n    if json {\n        let out = crate::format::with_warning(\n            serde_json::json!({ \"id\": id }),\n            warning.as_deref(),\n        );\n        println!(\"{}\", serde_json::to_string(&out)?);\n    } else {\n        println!(\"{}\", id);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn cmd_list(\n    beads_dir: &PathBuf,\n    status: Option<String>,\n    type_: Option<String>,\n    assignee: Option<String>,\n    priority: Option<i32>,\n    annotation: Option<String>,\n    limit: Option<usize>,\n    all: bool,\n    format: &str,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    // Parse annotation filter (key=value format)\n    let annotation_filter = match annotation {\n        Some(ref ann) => {\n            let parts: Vec<&str> = ann.splitn(2, '=').collect();\n            if parts.len() != 2 {\n                return Err(anyhow!(\"Invalid annotation format. Use key=value\"));\n            }\n            Some((parts[0].to_string(), parts[1].to_string()))\n        }\n        None => None,\n    };\n\n    let metadata = load_metadata(beads_dir)?;\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n    let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n\n    let mut issues = if all {\n        // Include archived beads\n        list_all_with_archives(beads_dir)?\n    } else {\n        // Only from database\n        let mut filter = IssueFilter::default();\n        if let Some(ref s) = status {\n            filter.status = Some(Status::from_str(s.as_str()).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref t) = type_ {\n            filter.issue_type =\n                Some(IssueType::from_str(t.as_str()).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?);\n        }\n        filter.assignee = assignee.clone();\n        filter.priority = priority;\n        filter.annotation = annotation_filter.clone();\n        // --limit 0 means unlimited\n        filter.limit = limit.and_then(|l| if l == 0 { None } else { Some(l) });\n        storage.list_issues(&filter)?\n    };\n\n    // Apply additional filters for --all mode (since we're not using DB filters)\n    if all {\n        if let Some(ref s) = status {\n            let status_filter = Status::from_str(s.as_str()).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?;\n            issues.retain(|i| i.status == status_filter);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref t) = type_ {\n            let type_filter = IssueType::from_str(t.as_str()).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?;\n            issues.retain(|i| i.issue_type == type_filter);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref assignee_val) = assignee {\n            issues.retain(|i| i.assignee.as_deref() == Some(assignee_val));\n        }\n        if let Some(p) = priority {\n            issues.retain(|i| i.priority.0 == p);\n        }\n        if let Some((ref key, ref value)) = annotation_filter {\n            issues.retain(|i| i.annotations.get(key).map_or(false, |v| v == value));\n        }\n        // Apply limit\n        if let Some(l) = The bf-5id blocked→open cascade must hold identically in the batch\nclose path.\n\n### 7.7 JSON contract discipline (P1)\n\n- One stable envelope shape for every command's `--json` output — fixes the\n  `bf ready` (JSON array) vs `bf list` (NDJSON) divergence that silently miscounts under\n  `json.load`.\n- `bf robot-docs`: machine-readable enumeration of every command's contract, for agent\n  consumers (NEEDLE worker prompts reference it instead of hardcoding shapes).\n\n### 7.8 Derived blocked status (P2 — architectural)\n\nUpstream computes blocked-ness from the dependency graph (with a `blocked_issues_cache`\ninvalidated on dep/close mutations) instead of storing a status that must be transitioned.\nThis deletes the bf-5id bug class (stuck-blocked beads stalling workers) at the root — the\njust-shipped cascade fix treats the symptom.\n\n**Hard constraint:** NEEDLE's safe-dispatch fences beads by manually setting\n`status=blocked`. A derived model MUST retain an explicit manual hold that presents as\nblocked and takes precedence over the derived value (dedicated flag or a preserved manual\nstatus — decide at design time, with NEEDLE-side review). CLI and JSONL compatibility:\nconsumers keep seeing `status: \"blocked\"`.\n\nIncludes a migration for existing stored-blocked rows.\n\n### 7.9 Multi-box & fleet concurrency (P2)\n\n- **Merge anchor** (`beads.base.jsonl`): a base snapshot enabling 3-way merge of JSONL\n  across checkouts — targets the recurring lab/ex44 divergence.\n- **Concurrent-writer hardening**: fleet-scale tests (N concurrent `bf` processes doing\n  create/claim/close) hunting the upstream-documented classes — parallel-write silent loss,\n  spurious sync conflicts during auto-import.\n- **Pre-export history backups** (`.bf_history/` with prune policy): one more insurance\n  layer under the JSONL, cheap to keep.\n\n### Non-goals\n\nUpstream surface deliberately NOT ported: the MCP server, workflow gates /\ntransition-scoped required fields, scheduler, agent-coordination module, epic containment,\ncapacity/admission control, and graph-analytics TUI. NEEDLE owns orchestration in this\nstack; `bv` exists for visualization; bf's identity is the lean, fleet-hardened store.\nPreserve bf's own differentiators upstream lacks: atomic `claim`, `critical_path`,\n`velocity`, `commit_check`, secret scanning, genesis beads, annotations.\n\n### Open questions\n\n- Auto-flush × rotation: incremental flush must target only the active `issues.jsonl`,\n  never archives — confirm rotation interplay before 7.1 ships.\n- Does auto-flush change git-commit cadence guidance for NEEDLE workers (`.beads/` will now\n  be dirty far more often between commits)?\n- 7.8 manual-hold representation (new flag vs preserved manual status) needs NEEDLE-side\n  review before implementation — do not start 7.8 until that decision is recorded here.\n\n---\n\n## Test Strategy & Isolation\n\nbf must be testable without touching, modifying, or interfering with any live `br` workspace. Three isolation concerns drive the test strategy:\n\n### Rule 1: Never Share a Live Database\n\nbf tests **never** auto-discover or open a `.beads/beads.db` that `br` is actively using. SQLite WAL mode serializes writers, so concurrent opens are safe from a corruption standpoint — but test mutations (creates, claims, closes) would contaminate real workspaces with spurious beads.\n\nAll tests target exactly one of:\n- **`:memory:`** — rusqlite in-memory database (unit tests, zero disk I/O)\n- **`tempfile::tempdir()`** — ephemeral directory deleted on drop (integration tests)\n- **Read-only fixture copy** — `issues.jsonl` copied out of a real workspace into a tempdir, never written back (compat tests)\n\n### Rule 2: Never Point `br` at a bf Test Database\n\nThe schema compat test must verify `br` can read a `bf`-created database — but it cannot use br's own workspace for this. The test creates a fresh tempdir, runs `bf init` + `bf create` in it, then invokes `br --db /path/to/temp/beads.db` against that file. The real `br` workspace is untouched.\n\n### Rule 3: JSONL Fixture = Read-Only Copy\n\nThe JSONL round-trip test uses a snapshot of a real workspace's `issues.jsonl` as a fixture, not a live file. The fixture is checked into `tests/fixtures/` (or copied at test time with `--allow-stale`). `bf sync --import` loads it into a tempdir database; `bf list --format json` is compared against the expected output derived from `br list --format json` run against the same snapshot.\n\n```\ntests/fixtures/\n├── forge-snapshot.jsonl    # snapshot of FORGE workspace (committed, static)\n└── needle-snapshot.jsonl   # snapshot of NEEDLE workspace\n```\n\nThese fixtures are updated manually when the schema changes: `cp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl tests/fixtures/forge-snapshot.jsonl`.\n\n### Test Harness (`tests/common/mod.rs`)\n\n```rust\npub struct TempWorkspace {\n    dir: tempfile::TempDir,   // deleted on drop — no cleanup needed\n    pub db_path: PathBuf,\n    pub storage: Storage,\n}\n\nimpl TempWorkspace {\n    pub fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n        let dir = tempfile::tempdir()?;\n        let db_path = dir.path().join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n        fs::create_dir(dir.path().join(\".beads\"))?;\n        let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n        Ok(Self { dir, db_path, storage })\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_fixture(jsonl: &Path) -> Result<Self> {\n        let ws = Self::new()?;\n        import_jsonl(jsonl, &ws.storage)?;\n        Ok(ws)\n    }\n\n    // Run br against this workspace's db (for compat tests)\n    pub fn br(&self, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {\n        Command::new(\"br\")\n            .arg(\"--db\").arg(&self.db_path)\n            .args(args)\n            .output()\n            .expect(\"br not in PATH\")\n    }\n}\n```\n\nUnit tests in `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `Storage::open(\":memory:\")` directly — no `TempWorkspace` needed.\n\n### Schema Forward-Compatibility","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}
